argument:
IHH's ex-exceptional profit grew 36% in Q2 and 22% in H1, while revenue and EBITDA grew 7% and 14% excluding MFRS129. That operating improvement provides a defensible growth purchase at 30.38x trailing and estimated 27.05x forward earnings, without relying on Turkish inflation accounting. Pre-financing FCF of RM771m confirms that hospital growth is producing some cash after asset investment.

The cushion is thin: net debt is RM11.564bn excluding RM2.205bn leases, and cash after specified financing and lease costs was only RM141m against RM486m owner dividends. Core growth makes servicing the expansion plausible, but payout restraint and better conversion may be necessary. Governance/legal statements cannot be dismissed or assigned invented outcomes. The weak price trend favors measured entry; upside depends on continued underlying hospital profitability rather than an assumed defensive-sector rerating.
key_points: Accounting-adjusted operating and profit growth support the core thesis.
Positive cash after investment provides a funding starting point.
Leverage, thin dividend coverage and governance events require discipline.
